title: Development is being shaped by interacting fractures in multilateral cooperation, conflict, digital capacity, debt, and civic trust
source_unit: UNDP, The Landscape of Development: UNDP Trends Update 2026
geography: Global development, multilateral cooperation, conflict, gender, health, digital systems, prosperity, migration, trust, debt, sustainable finance, energy, and environment

military_spending_change.unit: percent growth in global military expenditure from 2023 to 2024

military_spending_gdp.unit: percent of global GDP represented by military expenditure

oda_2024.unit: US dollars in official development assistance in 2024

oda_projected_change.unit: percent projected change in ODA from 2024 to 2025

support_international_cooperation.unit: percent of people reported as supporting international cooperation even when it requires compromising national interests

observations.method: UNDP Strategy and Futures Team synthesis of global development indicators, geopolitical trends, public-attitude evidence, and emerging policy signals.
observations.uncertainty: This is a cross-domain trends update rather than a harmonized causal dataset; figures use source-specific years, definitions, and methods and do not establish that military or aid changes caused public trust or development outcomes.
observations.subgroup: States, international organizations, donors, developing countries, populations affected by aid or security spending, and publics evaluating international cooperation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Security spending and new forms of cooperation can sometimes protect infrastructure, create human-security investment, or support a reconfigured rather than absent multilateral order.

denominator.unit: global state-based conflict and violence-impact frame

cross_border_conflict_involvement.unit: UN member states involved in conflicts beyond their borders, approximately 40 percent

violence_economic_impact.unit: US dollars of global economic impact of violence in 2024, approximately 12 percent of global GDP

conflict_exposure.unit: in 6 people exposed to conflict in 2025

prevention_return.unit: US dollars of possible conflict-related costs potentially saved per dollar invested in prevention, according to the report synthesis

observations.method: UNDP synthesis of conflict, violence, exposure, economic-cost, humanitarian, and prevention evidence.
observations.uncertainty: Global conflict counts and economic-cost estimates depend on definitions and source methods; the prevention range is modeled and does not identify a universal return on any particular intervention.
observations.subgroup: Civilians, states, non-state armed groups, host communities, humanitarian actors, workers, firms, and populations exposed to direct or spillover violence.
observations.counterinterpretation: Conflict exposure can decline in some places, and prevention, institutions, early warning, and peace agreements can reduce harm even while the global aggregate remains severe.

observations.period: 2025-2026; digital capacity, AI exposure, and identity infrastructure

denominator.unit: global digital development, AI, and identity-infrastructure frame

ai_job_exposure_advanced.unit: percent of jobs in advanced economies exposed to AI according to the report synthesis

ai_job_exposure_low_income.unit: percent of jobs in low-income countries exposed to AI according to the report synthesis

organizations_ai_agents.unit: percent of organizations across 105 countries experimenting with or scaling AI agents

no_digital_id.unit: people without access to a digital identity in 2025, approximately

no_legal_identity.unit: people lacking a legal identity, approximately

data_center_power_growth.unit: percent potential increase in global data-centre power demand by 2030

observations.method: UNDP synthesis of connectivity, AI exposure, organization adoption, digital public infrastructure, identity, and data-centre energy indicators.
observations.uncertainty: AI exposure is not job loss or realized productivity; adoption and digital identity counts do not establish usable access, safety, ownership, or service receipt, and the power estimate is a projection.
observations.subgroup: Offline populations, workers, public agencies, firms, women, low-income countries, people without legal identity, digital-platform users, and communities affected by data-centre infrastructure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital public infrastructure, open models, connectivity, and identity systems can expand access and state capacity if governance, privacy, affordability, and local capability keep pace.

denominator.unit: countries represented in the report's aggregate grievance and trust evidence

authoritarian_rule.unit: percent of people worldwide living under authoritarian rule according to the report synthesis

hybrid_authoritarian_tendency.unit: percent of people worldwide living in hybrid regimes with authoritarian tendencies

rule_of_law_decline.unit: percent of countries where rule-of-law conditions declined in 2025, compared with 57 percent in 2024

grievance.unit: percent of people across 26 countries with moderate or high grievance

protest_increase_countries.unit: countries where protest activity increased in 2025

hostile_activism_approval.unit: percent across 28 countries approving at least one form of hostile activism, according to the report synthesis

observations.method: UNDP synthesis of democracy, rule-of-law, grievance, protest, trust, and civic-participation indicators and public-attitude evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The reported aggregate attitudes and country counts do not establish that grievance caused protest, hostile activism, authoritarianism, or durable institutional change; country coverage and question wording vary by source.
observations.subgroup: Young people, national and local institutions, protesters, nonparticipants, marginalized groups, political actors, businesses, and publics evaluating fairness and voice.
observations.counterinterpretation: High grievance can coexist with constructive participation, local governance innovation, citizens' assemblies, and reforms that rebuild trust rather than produce destabilization.

related_sources.claim: Official UNDP publication page, date, purpose, and report provenance.
Related UNDP human-development horizon work on planetary systems and development.

boundary: This record adds an integrated development-landscape route linking multilateralism, conflict, digital capacity, identity, debt, energy, distrust, grievance, and civic action. It is a cross-domain public synthesis with source-specific aggregate indicators, not respondent-level evidence, a pooled causal model, individual political behavior, or proof that any reported trend caused a later outcome.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNDP Trends Update 2026 publication page and PDF were reviewed; multilateralism, conflict, digital capacity, AI exposure, identity, distrust, grievance, protest, and rule-of-law claims were cross-checked against the report's 12-theme structure.
